phase3_findings.description: The historical release-note entry for the earlier save_queries change, at line 73 of docs/external/release-notes.md, still says that SQL Lens "still saves free-form notes" when save_queries is off. This change removed exactly that clause from the matching row in docs/external/configuration.md, so the release-notes copy now states a promise the code no longer keeps. The line sits in a dated historical entry and the diff does not touch it. The two reviewers filed it with different kinds (documented_falsehood and comment_drift) but describe the same defect at the same file and line.

A blank or whitespace-only value for save_text_memories is turned into false with no log line or warning, at lines 221 to 230 of src/sqllens/config.py. An operator whose launcher expands an unset shell variable into SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES therefore gets note saving switched off silently, while a plain typo such as ture still fails loudly. The one case where the operator's intent is unclear is the one case with no diagnostic.

The internal readiness page docs/internal/production-readiness-v0.1.0.md, at line 70, still records that SaveTextMemoryTool is registered as a settled fact. After this change the tool is registered only when save_text_memories is on, so the unqualified sentence no longer holds for a default configuration. The file is a dated, point-in-time page and is outside this diff.

Line 30 of mcpb/manifest.json maps the environment variable to ${user_config.save_text_memories}. If an upgraded bundle install that has no stored value for this newly added field passes the placeholder through unreplaced, config loading raises a validation error and the server does not start, rather than falling back to off. The same shape already exists for read_only, so this is an existing pattern rather than something this change introduced.

The new tests at lines 253 to 276 of tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py assert only that the tool is absent and that the prompt section is missing. They do not pin the two further promises the factory comment makes for the flag-off path: that stored notes are still injected into the prompt, and that curated writes through MemoryStore.save_text_memory still go through. Those are the exact regressions the comment warns a future refactor could cause.

The test test_memory_admin_and_insecure_auth_are_not_exposed, at lines 51 to 61 of tests/unit/test_mcpb_manifest.py, pins the absence of settings unrelated to the behavior this change adds. It will fail and need editing on the day an unrelated change legitimately adds an admin-tools checkbox, with no real regression behind the failure. This is a maintenance cost rather than a defect.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (six suggestion-level findings, none at or above the critical threshold)

This pull request is ready to merge: every one of the forty-three checklist items passed, all five acceptance criteria are itemized and verified against the shipped code, and the six remaining findings are suggestions that no reviewer raised above suggestion level.

Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. The historical release-note entry for the earlier `save_queries` change, at line 73 of `docs/external/release-notes.md`, still says that SQL Lens "still saves free-form notes" when `save_queries` is off. This change removed exactly that clause from the matching row in `docs/external/configuration.md`, so the release-notes copy now states a promise the code no longer keeps. The line sits in a dated historical entry and the diff does not touch it. (raised by 2/5 agents)
2. A blank or whitespace-only value for `save_text_memories` is turned into `false` with no log line or warning, at lines 221 to 230 of `src/sqllens/config.py`. An operator whose launcher expands an unset shell variable into `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES` therefore gets note saving switched off silently, while a plain typo such as `ture` still fails loudly. The one case where the operator's intent is unclear is the one case with no diagnostic. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. The internal readiness page `docs/internal/production-readiness-v0.1.0.md`, at line 70, still records that `SaveTextMemoryTool` is registered as a settled fact. After this change the tool is registered only when `save_text_memories` is on, so the unqualified sentence no longer holds for a default configuration. The file is a dated, point-in-time page and is outside this diff. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. Line 30 of `mcpb/manifest.json` maps the environment variable to `${user_config.save_text_memories}`. If an upgraded bundle install that has no stored value for this newly added field passes the placeholder through unreplaced, config loading raises a validation error and the server does not start, rather than falling back to off. The same shape already exists for `read_only`, so this is an existing pattern rather than something this change introduced. (raised by 1/5 agents)
5. The new tests at lines 253 to 276 of `tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py` assert only that the tool is absent and that the prompt section is missing. They do not pin the two further promises the factory comment makes for the flag-off path: that stored notes are still injected into the prompt, and that curated writes through `MemoryStore.save_text_memory` still go through. Those are the exact regressions the comment warns a future refactor could cause. (raised by 1/5 agents)
6. The test `test_memory_admin_and_insecure_auth_are_not_exposed`, at lines 51 to 61 of `tests/unit/test_mcpb_manifest.py`, pins the absence of settings unrelated to the behavior this change adds. It will fail and need editing on the day an unrelated change legitimately adds an admin-tools checkbox, with no real regression behind the failure. This is a maintenance cost rather than a defect. (raised by 1/5 agents)

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With `save_text_memories` not set, as in a config file holding only settings that exist before this change, the config loads without error, `build_agent` registers no `save_text_memory` tool, and the system prompt built from that agent's tool list contains no "TEXT MEMORY" section. The same holds with `save_text_memories = false`, and with an empty or whitespace-only value, whether it comes from the environment variable `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES` or from `save_text_memories = ""` in the TOML file. Any other value that is not a boolean, such as `ture`, still fails config validation.
- [ ] `mcpb/manifest.json` declares a `user_config` field `save_text_memories` of type `boolean` with `"default": false` and `"required": false`, and its `server.mcp_config.env` sets `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES` to `${user_config.save_text_memories}`. Because that variable is always set for a bundle install, the checkbox value wins over any `save_text_memories` in a TOML file there. `mcpb/README.md`'s settings table has a row for the checkbox stating that it defaults to off.
- [ ] With `save_text_memories = true` in TOML, and separately with the environment variable `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES=true` and no TOML key, `build_agent` registers the `save_text_memory` tool as a `SaveTextMemoryTool`, and the system prompt built from that agent's tool list contains the "TEXT MEMORY" section.
- [ ] The first `## Unreleased` section of `docs/external/release-notes.md`, the one directly below the October 28, 2026 entry at the top of the page, has an entry that states the agent no longer saves free-form notes unless `save_text_memories = true`, marks this as a behavior change for existing deployments, and tells operators who configure SQL Lens with a TOML file or environment variables to set `save_text_memories = true` to keep the old behavior, and tells MCPB users to turn on the new checkbox in the extension's settings. It also says that free-form notes saved earlier stay in memory and are still used, that notes the agent saved cannot be told apart from notes added by an import, that operators who configure SQL Lens with a TOML file or environment variables can review the free-form notes and delete the wrong ones with the memory administration tools, linking the "Memory-Administration Tools for the Assistant" section of `docs/external/managing-memory.md` for how to enable them and what deleting requires, and that an MCPB install's settings offer no way to turn on those tools.
- [ ] The change leaves these as they are: the handling of unknown keys under `[memory]`, so a misspelled key such as `save_text_memory = true` is ignored and the tool stays unregistered; the system prompt sentence "Do NOT forget to save successful executions.", which still prints whenever the memory search tool is registered, including when no save tool is registered; the notes already in memory, none of which is deleted or changed, and the context enhancer still adds the matching ones to the system prompt; the metadata stored with a note, which still records nothing about whether the agent or an import wrote it; the `sqllens init` and Claude Desktop installer config templates, which do not list `save_text_memories`; and `mcpb/manifest.json`'s other settings, which still include nothing for `memory.allow_admin_tools` or `auth.insecure`.
